correctness.rationale: For inverse-image continuous star maps, the central target fiber is empty, a singleton, or an edge, and all other fibers must meet explicit disjoint face constraints. These cases are exhaustively listed, counted without overlaps and verify the displayed rank profile. Idempotency is equivalent to fixing every image point. Regularity is equivalent to a continuous fiberwise section; exactly an injective partial map with source center and at least one source leaf but leaf-only image fails to have a section. We checked this argument at all boundaries n>=1, k=0..n+1, and independently enumerated all 12,365 valid maps for n=1..5, matching every rank, idempotent and nonregular count. Finite tests are not a general proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 full text gives a graph-independent decomposition and only qualitative general regularity, and its explicit enumerations are for paths/cycles, not complete star profiles. The 2024 star-endomorphism paper uses forward graph maps, so its counts cannot dominate these inverse-image profiles. Published published-finding corpus searches, direct 2026/2020/2024 primary text comparisons, and accessible own prior claims found no equivalent exact rank, idempotent and nonregular star enumeration. Historical-priority risk remains, notably the abstract-only 2023 examples paper and unindexed older enumerations; this PASS is a qualified best-knowledge scientific judgment.

value.rationale: The star is the natural first branching tree after paths and cycles in the new graph-continuous monoid literature. The result computes complete rank profiles (not just order), all idempotents and the exact nonregular obstruction across an infinite family, meaningfully sharpening the already-known qualitative regularity theorem; the polynomial/binomial profiles isolate a concrete structural boundary relevant to monoid idempotents and generalized inverses. This is a natural complete classification, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
